t.1.20.1: Having heard those words of his, whose syllables were faltering with affection, Kauśika, filled with anger, spoke in reply to the lord of the earth.
t.1.20.2: Having first promised the thing, you now wish to abandon your pledge; this reversal is unfitting for the Rāghavas and for this lineage.
t.1.20.3: If this is what seems fitting to you, O king, I shall go back the way I came. Be happy with your kinsmen, O Kākutstha, you whose promise has proved false!
t.1.20.4: When the wise Viśvāmitra was seized with anger, the whole earth trembled, and fear entered the gods.
t.1.20.5: Perceiving that the whole world had become stricken with fear, the great sage Vasiṣṭha, steadfast and faithful to his vows, spoke these words to the king.
t.1.20.6: Born in the family of the Ikṣvākus, you are like a second Dharma incarnate; steadfast, faithful to your vows and glorious, you ought not to abandon dharma.
t.1.20.7: The Rāghava is renowned in the three worlds as one whose very self is dharma. Hold fast to your own dharma; you ought not to take on adharma.
t.1.20.8: O Rāghava, for one who promises, saying 'I will do so,' and then does not do it, there would be the destruction of all the merit of his sacrifices and pious works; therefore send Rāma forth.
t.1.20.9: Whether he is skilled in weapons or unskilled, the rākṣasas will not be able to overcome him while he is guarded by the son of Kuśika, just as amṛta is guarded by blazing fire.
t.1.20.10: He is dharma embodied, he is the foremost among the valiant; he surpasses all in the world in wisdom, and he is the supreme abode of austerity.
t.1.20.11: He knows the various divine weapons in the three worlds with all their moving and unmoving beings; no other man knows him truly, nor will any ever come to know him.
t.1.20.12: Neither the gods nor any of the sages, neither the Asuras nor the Rākṣasas, nor the foremost of the Gandharvas and Yakṣas, together with the Kiṃnaras and the great serpents.
t.1.20.13: All the astras, the supremely righteous sons of Kṛśāśva, were given long ago to Kauśika, when he was ruling the kingdom.
t.1.20.14: These too are the sons of Kṛśāśva, born of the daughters of Prajāpati: celestial in form, of great valour, radiant, and bringers of victory.
t.1.20.16: Long ago, she who is named Jayā obtained fifty excellent sons, immeasurable in might and able to assume any form at will, for the destruction of the armies of the asuras.
t.1.20.15: Jayā and Suprabhā, the slender-waisted daughters of Dakṣa, bring forth for you a hundred supremely radiant missiles and weapons.
t.1.20.17: And Suprabhā, moreover, gave birth to fifty more sons named the Saṃhāras, irresistible, unassailable and exceedingly mighty.
t.1.20.18: This son of Kuśika knows those weapons as they truly are, and he is able to create new ones never seen before; moreover, he is a knower of dharma.
t.1.20.19: Viśvāmitra, of great splendor and great austerity, is possessed of such prowess; O king, you should not fall into doubt about Rāma's going.
